why: The ticket changes the shape of a public response, and its own context lists a web client and a mobile client that read the old shape, yet it claims no other area is affected and calls the risk low. Both clients would break on release. An empty impact list is only acceptable when the change is plainly self-contained.

task.summary: Change the POST /signup success response from a bare user object to an envelope, {"data": {...user}}, to match the newer endpoints.

story.role: a support agent investigating accounts that cannot be found by name
story.benefit: no more accounts are created that nobody can search for or sign in to

task.goal: Wrap the signup success response in a data envelope.

acceptance.behavior: A successful signup returns 201 with the body {"data": user}, where user has the same fields as today.
acceptance.gherkin:
Given a valid signup request
When it is sent to POST /signup
Then the response status is 201
And the body is {"data": {"id": <new id>, "username": "ada", "email": "ada@example.com"}}

Given a signup request with an invalid email
When it is sent to POST /signup
Then the response is the same 422 body as before the change

testCases.description: POST /signup with a valid body returns 201 and a body whose only top-level key is data, containing id, username and email.
POST /signup with email "not-an-email" returns the existing 422 body byte for byte.

scenarios.omitted: Hidden scenarios are not implemented yet.

reuse: The validationError(code, message) helper in src/errors.js, which already produces the 422 error shape used by the email and password checks
